definitions.explanation: Strong sexual desire or craving, often with a negative or moralistic connotation. Originally a Buddhist term referring to one of the worldly desires that lead to suffering.

examples.japanese: {色欲|しきよく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{溺|おぼ}れる→溺れる：02026_oboreru⟧。
{色欲|しきよく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{仏教|ぶっきょう}→仏教：11428_bukkyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{煩悩|ぼんのう}→煩悩：14880_bonnou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Lust is considered one of the worldly desires in Buddhism.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{色欲|しきよく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧くらみ、⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{滅|ほろ}ぼした→滅ぼす：13332_horobosu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{伝|つた}えられている→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧。
examples.english: It is said that the king was blinded by lust and brought his kingdom to ruin.

notes:
A literary and somewhat formal term rooted in Buddhist philosophy. {色|しき} here refers to physical/sensory phenomena (particularly related to the body and sexuality), and ⟦{欲|よく}→欲：13183_yoku⟧ means desire or craving. In Buddhism, {色欲|しきよく} is one of the {五欲|ごよく} (five desires) that bind humans to the cycle of suffering.

In modern Japanese, the word carries a strong negative or moralizing tone and appears most often in literary, religious, or historical contexts rather than casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色欲|しきよく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{溺|おぼ}れる→溺れる：02026_oboreru⟧: to drown in lust
- {色欲|しきよく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧くらむ: to be blinded by lust
- {色欲|しきよく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抑|おさ}える→抑える：12806_osaeru⟧: to suppress lustful desires

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{性欲|せいよく}→性欲：23807_seiyoku⟧: sexual desire — neutral, clinical term without moral judgment
- ⟦{欲望|よくぼう}→欲望：05086_yokubou⟧: desire, craving — broader, covering all types of desire
- ⟦{煩悩|ぼんのう}→煩悩：14880_bonnou⟧: worldly desires — Buddhist term for all earthly cravings
